name: OpenChamber
description: OpenChamber is a web/PWA UI for the OpenCode AI coding agent. This script installs it natively via Node.js/npm on top of the OpenCode CLI in an LXC (no Docker) and runs it as a systemd service on port 3000 with a generated UI password.

notes.text: The web UI binds to 0.0.0.0:3000 and requires UI auth (binding to 0.0.0.0 without a password is not allowed upstream). A password is auto-generated at install, shown once on screen, and saved to /etc/openchamber/openchamber.env (mode 0600) as OPENCHAMBER_UI_PASSWORD — it never appears on the command line. Recover/change it in that file and restart the service: `systemctl restart openchamber`.
Web UI: http://<container-ip>:3000 (installable as a PWA). Unauthenticated health endpoint: http://<container-ip>:3000/health.

The OpenCode CLI is installed alongside (symlinked to /usr/local/bin/opencode). OpenChamber starts and manages its own OpenCode server — do not run a separate opencode service. Configure provider API keys inside the container with `opencode auth login` — stored at /root/.local/share/opencode/auth.json.

Update an existing container: run `update` inside the LXC, or `pct exec <CTID> -- update` from the Proxmox host. The updater upgrades the base system, re-runs the OpenCode installer (CLI upgrade), runs `npm install -g @openchamber/web@latest`, restarts the service, and waits for /health.
Unattended install with a custom UI password: `var_ui_password="your-secret" bash -c "$(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oraad/proxmox-scripts/main/ct/openchamber.sh)"`.
Debian only: OpenChamber requires Node.js >= 24.14.0, provided by the NodeSource APT-based setup_nodejs helper — there is no Alpine path. Service logs: `journalctl -u openchamber`.
